concepts.name: WEF: Foundational Identity and Legal Status
key_dimensions: Founded in 1971 by Klaus Schwab as European Management Forum; renamed WEF in 1987
Legal status: International organization for public-private cooperation — NOT a UN body, NOT an IGO
Headquartered in Cologny (Geneva), Switzerland — common trap: confused with Geneva city proper
Recognized by Swiss government as an international body under a 1971 framework agreement

concepts.name: Annual Davos Meeting: Structure and Significance
key_dimensions: Held annually in Davos-Klosters, Switzerland — typically in January
Participants: Heads of state, CEOs, central bank governors, civil society, academia — multi-stakeholder model
Agenda-setting role vs. decision-making power: WEF sets discourse but has no binding authority
Special/Emergency meetings sometimes held outside Davos (e.g., 2022 postponed due to COVID)

concepts.name: Global Competitiveness Report (GCR): Methodology and Indices
key_dimensions: Measures national competitiveness across 12 pillars including institutions, infrastructure, macroeconomic environment, ICT adoption
GCI 4.0 introduced in 2018 to incorporate 4th Industrial Revolution factors — shift from input-based to productivity-based measurement
GCR was suspended in 2020 (COVID) and replaced by Special Edition reports — UPSC trap: India's rank cannot be compared across years seamlessly
Distinction: GCR ≠ Ease of Doing Business (World Bank) ≠ IMD World Competitiveness Yearbook — overlapping but different methodologies

concepts.name: Global Gender Gap Report (GGGR): Four Pillars and India's Performance
key_dimensions: Four sub-indices: Economic Participation & Opportunity, Educational Attainment, Health & Survival, Political Empowerment
Measures gender parity (0 = imparity, 1 = parity), NOT absolute well-being levels — common conceptual trap
India typically ranks low on Economic Participation but scores high on Political Empowerment due to female heads of state history
Distinction from UNDP Gender Inequality Index (GII) and Gender Development Index (GDI) — different methodologies and publishers

concepts.name: Global Risks Report: Categories and Framework
key_dimensions: Published annually before Davos; classifies risks by likelihood and impact over 2-year and 10-year horizons
Five risk categories: Economic, Environmental, Geopolitical, Societal, Technological
Recent top risks: Climate action failure, Weapons of mass destruction, Cost-of-living crisis, Erosion of social cohesion
Based on Global Risks Perception Survey (GRPS) — input from WEF community, not independent research — important methodological caveat

concepts.name: Global Travel and Tourism Competitiveness Index (TTCI)
key_dimensions: Rebranded as Travel & Tourism Development Index (TTDI) in 2021 — UPSC may use either name
Five pillars: Enabling Environment, T&T Policy, Infrastructure, Natural & Cultural Resources, T&T Demand Conditions
India's rank improvement driven by natural resources, cultural heritage, price competitiveness — versus weaknesses in safety, health, hygiene
Distinction from UNWTO data and Tourism Competitiveness under GCR — separate publication

concepts.name: Energy Transition Index (ETI): Concept and India's Position
key_dimensions: Measures country performance on energy triangle: Energy Security, Energy Equity (access & affordability), Environmental Sustainability
Also assesses 'readiness' for transition — distinguishes current performance from future preparedness
India consistently cited for strong transition momentum despite lower absolute score — relevant to India's energy diplomacy
Distinction from IEA Energy Security index and IRENA metrics — different publishers and focus areas

concepts.name: Future of Jobs Report: Key Concepts
key_dimensions: Published biennially; forecasts job creation and displacement due to automation, AI, and green transition
Introduces concepts like 'reskilling imperative' and 'double disruption' (automation + COVID)
Identifies fastest-growing roles (data analysts, AI specialists, green economy jobs) vs. declining roles (data entry, accounting clerks)
Relevant to India's National Education Policy linkages and skill development policy discourse

concepts.name: Global Human Capital Report: Distinction from HDI
key_dimensions: Measures human capital development across four dimensions: Capacity, Deployment, Development, Know-how
Five age cohorts used (0–14, 15–24, 25–54, 55–64, 65+) — lifecycle approach, different from UNDP HDI
HDI (UNDP) focuses on outcomes (income, education, health); WEF HCI focuses on economic deployment potential
World Bank also publishes Human Capital Index — three different 'human capital' indices from three different bodies is a classic UPSC trap

concepts.name: Inclusive Development Index (IDI): Alternative to GDP
key_dimensions: Proposed as alternative to GDP for measuring economic progress — three pillars: Growth & Development, Inclusion, Intergenerational Equity
Discontinued after 2018 — important trap: questions may reference it as current WEF publication
Distinguished from IMF's concept of inclusive growth and World Bank's Shared Prosperity indicator
Highlights WEF's advocacy role in redefining development metrics beyond traditional GDP-centric approach

concepts.name: Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR): WEF's Conceptual Framework
key_dimensions: Concept coined by Klaus Schwab; characterizes fusion of physical, digital, biological domains — distinct from 3IR (digital revolution)
WEF established Centre for the Fourth Industrial Revolution (C4IR) — India hosts a C4IR node in Mumbai (partnership with Government of India)
Policy areas: AI governance, drone regulations, blockchain, precision medicine — WEF as norm-setter, not regulator
Distinction: 4IR ≠ Industry 4.0 (German manufacturing concept) — often confused in MCQs

concepts.name: WEF's Centre for the Fourth Industrial Revolution (C4IR) — India Node
key_dimensions: India's C4IR established in Mumbai in 2018 — one of the first national nodes globally
Focus areas for India: AI policy, drones, precision agriculture, data governance
Operated in partnership with NITI Aayog and Ministry of Electronics & IT (MeitY)
WEF C4IR network ≠ WEF headquarters — decentralized structure important for factual questions

concepts.name: WEF's Stakeholder Capitalism vs. Shareholder Capitalism
key_dimensions: WEF's 2020 Davos Manifesto redefined corporate purpose: companies should serve all stakeholders, not just shareholders
Contrasts with Milton Friedman's shareholder primacy doctrine — WEF positioned as normative counterpoint
Related to ESG (Environmental, Social, Governance) frameworks which WEF actively promotes
Relevant to UPSC questions on corporate governance, CSR mandate under Companies Act, and global business ethics

concepts.name: WEF and Global Health: Pandemic Preparedness Role
key_dimensions: WEF co-hosts CEPI (Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations) funding discussions — but CEPI itself is a separate body
WEF's 'Pandemic Preparedness' reports distinct from WHO's IHR framework — advisory vs. binding
WEF–Johns Hopkins partnership on global health security indices — input into Global Health Security Index
WEF has no enforcement mechanism — purely convening and agenda-setting role in health governance

concepts.name: WEF Reports vs. Other International Reports: Comparison Matrix
key_dimensions: Global Competitiveness Report (WEF) vs. Ease of Doing Business (World Bank — discontinued 2021) vs. IMD Competitiveness (IMD Lausanne)
Gender Gap Report (WEF) vs. GII (UNDP) vs. GDI (UNDP) — different metrics, publishers, and India's relative rankings differ
Global Risks Report (WEF) vs. World Risk Report (Bündnis Entwicklung Hilft) vs. Fragile States Index (Fund for Peace)
Energy Transition Index (WEF) vs. Energy Security Index (IEA) vs. SDG7 tracking (UN) — classic one-liner trap in prelims

concepts.name: WEF's Financing Mechanisms and Funding Model
key_dimensions: Funded by membership fees from ~1,000 member companies (global multinationals with >USD 5 billion revenue typically)
NOT funded by governments or UN system — private-sector-led multilateral forum
Strategic Partners and Industry Partners tiers — companies pay to engage in agenda-shaping
Criticism: elite capture, lack of democratic accountability — relevant to governance and global institutions questions

concepts.name: WEF's Great Reset Initiative
key_dimensions: Launched in June 2020 as post-COVID recovery framework — three pillars: fair markets, equitable outcomes, Fourth Industrial Revolution
Aligned with UN SDGs and Paris Agreement — WEF positioned as bridge between private sector and multilateral goals
Distinguished from IMF's 'Great Lockdown' terminology and World Bank's recovery frameworks
Criticized from both left (insufficient redistribution) and right (overreach of global elites) — balance of perspectives important for essay/mains

concepts.name: WEF and India: Strategic Engagement and Reports
key_dimensions: India hosts WEF India Economic Summit annually — separate from Davos, held in India
C4IR Mumbai node, India-WEF collaboration on skill development, digital public infrastructure advocacy
India's performance across WEF indices: typically strong in market size pillar of GCI, weak in health and gender indices
WEF has highlighted India's UPI and Aadhaar as global models for digital public infrastructure — relevant to tech diplomacy questions

concepts.name: WEF's Role in Global Governance: Strengths and Criticisms
key_dimensions: Strengths: Multi-stakeholder convening, agenda-setting, norm entrepreneurship, bridging public-private sectors
Criticisms: Democratic deficit, unaccountable to citizens, dominated by Western and corporate interests
WEF ≠ G20, OECD, UN — no intergovernmental mandate, no binding decisions — purely soft power
Concept of 'Forum Shopping': states and corporations use WEF to advance positions outside formal multilateral channels

concepts.name: Global Financial Inclusion and WEF's Financial Development Report
key_dimensions: Financial Development Report assessed depth, access, and efficiency of financial systems — discontinued but may appear in static questions
WEF's work on financial inclusion intersects with World Bank Findex data and G20 Financial Inclusion agenda
Distinction: WEF Financial Development Report vs. IMF Financial Soundness Indicators vs. World Bank Global Findex
Relevant to India's JAM trinity (Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile) and financial inclusion policy discourse in mains answers
